title: Add benchmark-lab representative workload runners + reporting pipeline v47
author: Asha Kapoor
release_notes: Added representative workload runners for conversational summarization and long-context streaming profiles; reporting pipeline v47 uploads aggregated metrics to S3 and updates dashboards.
description:
Motivation: add two representative workload runners (conversational summarization and long-context streaming) to the benchmark-lab suite and wire them into the reporting pipeline v47 so we collect stable profiling baselines across model variants. This enables automated regression detection and provides representative latency/cost tradeoff traces for the Optimize team.

What this PR does: - Adds workload runners: benchmark-lab/runners/conversational_summarization and benchmark-lab/runners/long_context_streaming. Each runner includes synthetic traffic generators, seed prompt sets, and a small harness for deterministic warmup to produce repeatable cold/warm startup profiles. - Adds profiling baselines artifacts and example config for capturing KV-cache hit distributions and token-level latency histograms. - Implements reporting pipeline v47: a new Airflow DAG (jobs/benchmark_reporting/dags/report_v47.py) that aggregates runner outputs, normalizes latency/throughput metrics, and uploads artifacts to the metrics S3 bucket. - CI: expands the perf-canary GH workflow to run lightweight smoke runs of the new runners on PRs and on master nightly. - Docs: adds a README and runbook for the benchmark-lab runners and reporting pipeline, and updates the dashboard JSON that the Console team uses to display v47 metrics.

Checklist: - [x] Add representative runners and unit tests - [x] Add DAG and reporting transformation - [x] Add CI smoke tests and workflow updates - [x] Add docs and runbook - [x] Validate pipelines end-to-end on perf-canary staging

Testing & verification: ran the new runners in perf-canary with a small dedicated GPU instance and captured consistent baselines over 10 runs. The reporting DAG was executed in staging and the aggregated CSV/artifacts were uploaded and ingested by the dashboard generation job. Observability hooks (trace IDs and token-level histograms) were validated with local sample payloads.

Rollout plan: merge to main -> deploy reporting DAG to staging -> run 48h canary with two model variants -> if no regression, enable nightly baseline capture and include v47 in release notes.

Notes: kept runner implementations pluggable so future workloads can reuse the harness. No breaking API changes to the benchmark-lab runner interface.

Asha Kapoor: Added exponential backoff with jitter and retried uploads up to 5 times. Recorded trace IDs on failures to aid debugging.
Noah Patel: The warmup sequence timing looks conservative — can we reduce to speed up CI? Also add a smoke-only fast path for CI runs.
Asha Kapoor: Added FAST_WARMUP flag and reduced sampling in CI mode; kept default conservatively for nightly baselines.
Sofia Martinez: Tests look good but ensure the DAG has idempotent outputs to avoid double-counting when retried.
Asha Kapoor: Aggregation step now writes to a per-run prefix and an atomic manifest so retries are safe.
Liam Chen: CI initially failed on lint and type checks; fixed by tightening typing in utils.py and reformatting imports. CI green on rerun.
notes_other: CI: perf-canary smoke runs included in PR status; nightly job on main will produce full baselines.
